title: Reels bulk trim actions
problem: Creators had to trim clips one at a time, making long edits slow and error-prone.
evidence: 78% of tested creators expected multi-select trim; edit sessions averaged 4.2 min for batch work.
recommendation: Introduce multi-select with a bulk trim bar and clear selection state before building advanced timeline features.
outcome: Blocked downstream timeline work until the interaction model is agreed; prototype validated with the Reels panel.

title: Explore topic filtering
problem: Users could not filter Explore results by topic cluster, forcing manual scanning of long grids.
evidence: Ranking limitation surfaced during research; 6 of 8 participants abandoned the task.
recommendation: Resolve the taxonomy constraint before shipping the redesigned Explore filter panel.
outcome: Flagged as a blocker to the Explore redesign; engineering scoping in progress.

title: Spark AI confidence labels
problem: Creators could not judge how much to trust AI caption suggestions, reducing adoption of Spark AI.
evidence: Panel sessions showed hesitation and repeated manual rewriting of AI output.
recommendation: Add confidence labels, edit previews, and fallback states to an already-shipping surface.
outcome: Enhanced a live experience; trust and repeat usage improved in follow-up testing.

title: Sign-up flow rework
problem: Account creation had a high drop-off rate, limiting new user activation.
evidence: Funnel analysis showed a 34% drop at the username step.
recommendation: Rework the step sequencing and guidance on the current sign-up flow.
outcome: Enhanced a high-traffic flow; drop-off reduced in the redesigned path.

title: Quantifying UX dashboard
problem: Leadership had no consistent way to see UX's contribution, so its impact stayed invisible in planning conversations.
evidence: Monthly reviews relied on anecdotes; there was no shared view of research coverage, delivery, and influence.
recommendation: Build a single dashboard that quantifies UX contribution across research, delivery, and business impact.
outcome: Enhanced how leadership sees UX; contribution is now legible and tracked month over month.

title: Making Prism AI-ready
problem: AI-assisted design drifts from Prism because tokens carry values without usage intent — agents make logical-but-wrong choices.
evidence: Components meant to be identical diverge across screens; agents read values but not when or why to apply them.
recommendation: Structure Prism in three layers: tokens, intent metadata, and guardrail docs that constrain agent decisions.
outcome: Early opportunity to make the system agent-ready, cutting AI-generated design debt across sessions.

title: Stories creation zero-state
problem: New creators faced an empty Stories camera with no guidance on where to start.
evidence: Early concept testing surfaced confusion and low first-session publish success.
recommendation: Explore zero-state patterns and example templates as a new capability.
outcome: New opportunity to improve first-run experience; concept validated for further investment.

title: Safety notification patterns
problem: Users felt anxious interpreting account restriction messages presented in technical language.
evidence: Qualitative sessions surfaced repeated confusion and elevated task stress.
recommendation: Prototype plain-language safety patterns as a new, unmet-need direction.
outcome: Opportunity to reduce user anxiety; early patterns tested positively.

title: Creator Studio panel groupings
problem: Dense Creator Studio screens forced heavy scrolling, slowing creators during high-volume publishing.
evidence: Session recordings showed repeated long scrolls to reach common panels; task time suffered.
recommendation: Regroup studio panels by frequency and task, collapsing rarely used sections.
outcome: Optimization that cut scrolling and sped up common publishing tasks.

title: Cross-product design tokens
problem: Inconsistent spacing and color across Instagram surfaces slowed delivery and review.
evidence: Audit found 40+ divergent values for the same intent across teams.
recommendation: Standardize a shared Prism token set to simplify and speed up existing work.
outcome: Reduced rework and sped up handoff across Feed, Reels, and DMs teams.

title: Activity center consolidation
problem: Notifications were spread across surfaces, adding noise and maintenance overhead.
evidence: Support tickets cited duplicate and conflicting alerts for likes, mentions, and follows.
recommendation: Consolidate into one activity center to simplify the existing experience.
outcome: Simplified the surface and reduced duplicate alerts.
